# Two identically written actions are two mutants, not one.
#
# An action is identified for reuse by its template, its text and the
# types resolved for it. On its own that does not tell {{.Name}} in one
# place from {{.Name}} in another, so the second would find the first's
# verdict recorded and take it instead of being run -- reporting a kill it
# never earned, which is the sort of lie the skip machinery exists to
# avoid.
#
# TestPage looks only at the first occurrence. Emptying that one is caught;
# emptying the second changes nothing it asserts on and survives. The two
# must therefore reach different verdicts.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

# Running again reuses both verdicts, and they are still different ones. A
# single recorded verdict answering for both actions would show here as two
# alike: the second recording would have replaced the first.
muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want-reused.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}<a>{{.Name}}</a><b>{{.Name}}</b>{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Name string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Name: "x"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(buf.String(), "<a>x</a>") {
		t.Errorf("page = %q", buf.String())
	}
}
-- want.txt --
